mainTopic: Where רב's rule comes from (losing תרומה and being unfit for כהונה after relations with an unfit man), whom it covers, and which men trigger it.
overview: This amud continues an earlier discussion of רב's rule. A woman who has relations with a man who is unfit for her loses her right to eat תרומה and becomes unfit to marry a כהן. רב learns this from the פסוק "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר". First the גמרא checks that this פסוק is not already used up. It shows that the 'זר' verses and the extra words "בתרומת הקדשים" leave room for רב's rule. Next it finds a source to include a לויה and ישראלית: the extra word "ובת", which works even for the רבנן. A long back-and-forth follows about which source teaches תרומה and which teaches כהונה. It ends with "ובת" for תרומה and a קל וחומר from a גרושה for כהונה. That קל וחומר is allowed because it only reveals the reach of an existing ban. The גמרא then rejects limiting the rule to חייבי כריתות, since "כי תהיה" speaks of men she can actually marry. When it asks about a גוי or an עבד, it points to a separate teaching of רבי ישמעאל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: That verse is needed for its own basic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the general verse about a זר eating holy food is already needed to forbid an ordinary non-כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that verse is needed for its own plain meaning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the general verse "וכל זר לא יאכל קדש" can also cover the בת כהן married to a זר. It says that verse is already busy teaching that a regular non-כהן may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא hoped the law about a married בת כהן could come from the general זר verse. That would leave "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" free for רב's rule. The objection is that the general verse is fully used for its basic subject, the non-כהן himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a verse is already used for another teaching)
For itself, for its own plain subject
An outsider, meaning someone who is not a כהן

phrases.english: That one is needed for itself!
phrases.notes: "That one" is the פסוק "וכל זר לא יאכל קדש" (ויקרא 22:10). It is needed to forbid a plain non-כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the earlier discussion and challenges the suggested source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the general זר verse can also teach the law of a בת כהן married to a זר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse that is fully used for its own plain subject cannot also be used for another law.

steps.title: There are two 'וכל זר' verses
steps.stepSummary: The Torah writes 'וכל זר' twice, so one teaches about the non-כהן and the other about the married בת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two verses saying 'וכל זר' are written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out that the Torah says "וכל זר" two separate times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One "וכל זר" forbids a regular non-כהן. The second one is left over to teach about the בת כהן married to a זר. This leaves "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" free for רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
Are written (in the תורה)

phrases.english: Two "and any common man" verses are written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a second, extra verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought there was only one 'וכל זר' verse, and it was already used up.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two such verses, so one is free for the married בת כהן.

steps.title: The second verse is needed for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The extra 'וכל זר' is needed to teach that only being a זר forbids תרומה, not being an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said: 'וכל זר' means I told you that זרות forbids, but not אנינות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again: the second "וכל זר" is not free. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא uses it to teach that a mourner on the day of death (an אונן) may still eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads the verse as saying that only 'זרות', being a non-כהן, makes someone unfit for תרומה. אנינות does not. If the extra verse is used for this, it cannot also teach about the married בת כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: And still, but yet (introduces another objection)
Being a non-כהן
The state of an אונן, a mourner on the day a close relative died

phrases.english: But it is still needed
for the teaching of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina,
as Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
"And any common man": being a common man is what I told you,
phrases.notes: The Torah is speaking here: only being a non-כהן is what forbids you.

phrases.english: and not being a mourner!

steps.triggerLanguage: ואכתי מיבעי ליה לכדרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2 by finding another use for the extra verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the second 'וכל זר' is free
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second verse is already used by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא to exclude an אונן, so it is not free.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns from the extra word 'וכל'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's law comes from the extra 'וכל', not from the verse as a whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching comes from the difference between 'זר' and 'וכל זר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא does not need the whole verse. He learns his law from the extra word "וכל".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written just "זר". The added "וכל" is extra, and that extra word gives רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא his teaching about אנינות. So the verse itself is still free for the married בת כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out, it is learned from
From

phrases.english: That of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina
comes from "common man" versus "and any common man."
phrases.notes: Just 'זר' would have been enough. The extra 'וכל' is where his teaching comes from.

steps.triggerLanguage: דרבי יוסי ברבי חנינא מן זר וכל זר נפקא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning one law from an extra word and the other from the verse itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא needed the whole extra verse.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only needs the extra word 'וכל', so the verse is still free.
steps.whatToRemember: The two 'וכל זר' verses cover the non-כהן, the married בת כהן, and (through the extra 'וכל') רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's rule. So "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" can still be used for רב.

steps.title: The verse is needed to forbid חזה ושוק after she returns
steps.stepSummary: The verse "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" is needed to teach that a returning בת כהן may eat תרומה but not חזה ושוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed for what a ברייתא teaches: when she returns, she goes back to eating תרומה but not חזה ושוק. And רב חסדא said in the name of רבינא בר רב שילא: What is the verse? As it says, 'And a כהן's daughter who is married to a זר, she may not eat of the תרומת הקדשים.' This means she may not eat what is set apart from קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges once more, now attacking the verse רב himself uses. It says this verse is already needed for a ברייתא's law about a בת כהן who returns to her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that a בת כהן whose non-כהן husband died may go back to eating תרומה, but she may never again eat חזה ושוק. רב חסדא, quoting רבינא בר רב שילא, finds the source in this very verse: 'she may not eat of what is set apart from קדשים.' If the verse is used for this, it seems it cannot also be the source for רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches
Returns, goes back (to her father's house)
The breast and thigh of a שלמים offering, given to the כהן
What is the verse? What is the source?
What is set apart from holy offerings for the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תרומה (produce given to a כהן) with חזה ושוק (parts of an animal offering). The returning daughter gets back תרומה but never gets back חזה ושוק.

phrases.english: But it is still needed for what was taught:
phrases.notes: "It" now means רב's own verse, "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר."

phrases.english: When she returns, she returns to eating teruma,
but she does not return to eating the breast and thigh.
And Rav Ḥisda said
that Ravina son of Rav Sheila said:
What is the verse? As it is written:
"And if a priest's daughter is married to a common man,
she may not eat of the separated portion of the holy things":
she may not eat what is set apart from the holy offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'וכל זר' verses are settled, attacks רב's own verse directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's use of "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" as his source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That verse is already used, according to רב חסדא, to forbid חזה ושוק to a returning בת כהן, so it is not free for רב.

steps.title: The extra words teach two laws
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written 'בקדשים'. The longer phrase 'בתרומת הקדשים' teaches two things.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse write 'she may not eat of the קדשים.' Why does it say 'of the תרומת הקדשים'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse has extra wording, so it can teach both laws at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse only meant to forbid חזה ושוק, a shorter phrase, "בקדשים", would have been enough. The added word "תרומת" points to תרומה too. So the verse teaches both רב's rule about תרומה and the law of חזה ושוק.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the verse write
Learn two things from it

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write:
"She may not eat of the holy things."
Why does it say "of the separated portion of the holy things"?
Learn from it two things.

steps.triggerLanguage: אם כן לכתוב קרא היא בקדשים לא תאכל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and closes this line of questions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the verse teaches a second law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the verse only forbade חזה ושוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra word 'תרומת' lets the verse teach both laws, so רב's source stands.
steps.whatToRemember: When a verse uses more words than it needs, the גמרא often learns an extra law from them. Here 'בתרומת הקדשים' instead of 'בקדשים' teaches two things, so רב's rule about תרומה still has a source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves רב's source. It shows how one verse can carry two separate laws when its wording is longer than needed.

steps.title: What about a לויה or ישראלית?
steps.stepSummary: We have a source for a כהנת. Where is the source for a לויה or ישראלית?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for a כהנת. From where do we know the same for a לויה or ישראלית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the source it found for a בת כהן. Now it asks whether the same law applies to a לויה or ישראלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר' talks only about a priest's daughter. A לויה or ישראלית can also become connected to תרומה, for example by marrying a כהן. So the גמרא needs a separate source to include them in the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: We found (a source for this case)
A woman from a כהן family
A woman from a לוי family
A woman from an ordinary ישראל family
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We found a source for a priest's daughter;
a Levite or Israelite woman, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: a לויה or ישראלית who had relations with a man forbidden to her. Does she also lose the right to eat תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the source for a בת כהן now settled, the גמרא extends the question to other women.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that applies the rule to a לויה and ישראלית.

steps.title: The extra 'and' in 'ובת' includes them
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אבא in the name of רב, the extra ו in 'ובת' adds the לויה and ישראלית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבא said in the name of רב: the verse could have said 'בת' but says 'ובת'. Here too, 'בת' versus 'ובת' teaches the extra women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by using a method taught by רבי אבא in the name of רב. The verse says 'ובת', 'and a daughter', instead of just 'בת', and that extra letter ו adds more women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added ו means 'and', which hints that more cases are included. Here it widens the rule beyond a priest's daughter to a לויה and ישראלית.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Daughter' compared with 'and a daughter'. The extra ו adds more cases.
Here too

phrases.english: As Rabbi Abba said that Rav said:
'Daughter', 'and a daughter';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13. The verse begins 'ובת', with an extra ו, when 'בת' alone would have been enough.

phrases.english: here too: 'daughter', 'and a daughter'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra ו in 'ובת' includes a לויה and a ישראלית.

steps.title: Does this work only for רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: Learning from an extra ו is the method of רבי עקיבא. Does that mean this source works only for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? Is it only רבי עקיבא's, since he learns laws from the letter ו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Learning a law from a single extra ו is known as the method of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the source works only by learning from a ו, then the רבנן, who do not learn from extra letters like that, would have no source. The law would then be left as only one opinion's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Following whose opinion?
He learns laws from the letter ו ('and')

phrases.english: Whose view is this? Rabbi Akiva's,
since he learns laws from the letter vav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method used in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the law from the extra ו in 'ובת'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only רבי עקיבא learns from a ו, so the source would not work for the רבנן.

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree: the whole phrase is extra
steps.stepSummary: The entire phrase 'ובת' is extra, so even the רבנן can learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows the רבנן. The whole phrase 'ובת' is extra in the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source is not just the letter ו. The whole word 'ובת' is extra, and even the רבנן learn from an extra word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse before this one already spoke about a priest's daughter. So mentioning the daughter again is entirely extra, not just one letter. The רבנן do not learn from a lone ו, but they do learn from a whole extra phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
The Sages who disagree with רבי עקיבא
An extra, seemingly unneeded part of a verse

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis:
the whole phrase 'and a daughter' is extra in the verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the source: the whole word is extra, not just the letter.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source depended only on the extra ו, which only רבי עקיבא uses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole phrase 'ובת' is extra, so everyone agrees with the derivation.
steps.whatToRemember: A לויה and ישראלית are included in the rule through the extra 'ובת', and this works even for the רבנן.

steps.title: What about marrying a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: We have a source for תרומה. Where is the source that she may not marry into כהונה?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for תרומה. For marrying into כהונה, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. The source so far covers losing the right to eat תרומה. What tells us that a לויה or ישראלית in this situation may not marry a כהן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the right to eat תרומה and being forbidden to marry a כהן are two separate laws. A source for one does not automatically give us the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce, which a כהן and his household may eat
Here: marrying a כהן

phrases.english: We found a source for terumah;
for the priesthood, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know she is forbidden to marry a כהן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the law of תרומה to the law of כהונה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that she may not marry a כהן.

steps.title: The extra word must be about marrying a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counters that the extra word was surely about כהונה, since these women do not eat תרומה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say we did not include the לויה and ישראלית regarding כהונה? If it were about תרומה, are they women who eat תרומה at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a pushback question. The extra 'ובת' must already be teaching about marrying a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לויה or ישראלית does not normally eat תרומה, so including her in a rule about losing תרומה seems pointless. That suggests the extra word was really teaching that she may not marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (a pushback question)
We include (from an extra word)
Women who are allowed to eat תרומה

phrases.english: Is that to say that the Levite and Israelite woman
were not included by us regarding the priesthood?
For if it were regarding terumah,
are they women who eat terumah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ לְוִיָּה וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית לָא לִכְהוּנָּה מְרַבֵּינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by reading the derivation of step 8 as being about כהונה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra 'ובת' already teaches the law of כהונה, because these women do not eat תרומה anyway.

steps.title: She can eat תרומה because of her son
steps.stepSummary: The pushback is rejected. A ישראלית can eat תרומה through a son she has from a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? You can find her eating תרומה because of her son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the argument of the last step. There is a case where a לויה or ישראלית does eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראלית who was married to a כהן and has a son from him eats תרומה because of that son. So including her in a rule about losing תרומה makes sense. That means the source may be about תרומה only, and the question about כהונה comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not?
You can find such a case
Because of her son

steps.confusionAlert: Step 12 claimed that a לויה or ישראלית never eats תרומה on her own, apart from marrying a כהן. The case of her son from a כהן shows that she can, and that is why the argument falls apart.

phrases.english: Why not?
You find her eating terumah because of her son.
phrases.notes: Picture a ישראלית who had a son with a כהן. Because of that son, she is allowed to eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה לָא, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דְּקָאָכְלָה בִּשְׁבִיל בְּנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the argument of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the extra word must be about כהונה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A לויה or ישראלית can eat תרומה because of her son, so a rule about תרומה is not pointless for her.
steps.whyThisMatters: This puts the question of step 11 back on the table: we still need a source for the law of כהונה.

steps.title: Not eating through her son comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends its claim from step 12. The rule about eating through her son does not need the extra word, because a קל וחומר from a כהנת teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that she cannot eat because of her son comes from a קל וחומר. A כהנת eats תרומה because of her own holiness, and this act still disqualifies her. So a לויה or ישראלית, who eats only because of her son, should surely be disqualified too.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 13 pointed out that a ישראלית can eat תרומה through her son, so the extra word might be needed for that. Here the גמרא replies that we do not need the extra word for this, because logic already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman with strong, personal holiness loses her right to eat, a woman with only borrowed rights through her son should lose them even more easily. If this works, the extra word ״ובת״ is free to teach the ban on marrying into כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical argument: if the stricter case has this rule, the lighter case surely does
A כהן's daughter
A לוי's daughter and a ישראל's daughter
Because of her son (her son is a כהן)

phrases.english: Because of her son — that comes from a kal vachomer:
phrases.notes: He means that her not eating תרומה through her son comes from logic, not from the extra word.

phrases.english: Just as a priest's daughter,
who eats through her own holiness
— it disqualifies her,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the forbidden act of relations with an unfit man.

phrases.english: a Levite's or Israelite's daughter,
who eats only because of her son
— is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 13 by giving a separate source for the son case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate source: logic covers the son case, so the extra word stays free.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word might be needed to teach that she cannot eat through her son.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קל וחומר from a כהנת teaches the son case, so the extra word can teach the ban on כהונה.

steps.title: The קל וחומר works the other way
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is rejected. The holiness of a כהנת is the very reason she is disqualified, and a ישראלית does not have that holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: That very point argues the opposite. A כהנת, whose body is holy, is disqualified. This woman's body is not holy, so she is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר from step 14 using its own reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personal holiness is something that can be damaged. A woman who has no holiness of her own has nothing to lose, so the comparison breaks. That means the extra word is needed again for the son case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That very point gives the opposite': the reason for the argument actually works against it
Her body itself is holy

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying a ישראלית may eat through her son. It only says logic cannot prove she may not, so we need the extra word for that.

phrases.english: But that very point leads the other way:
a priest's daughter, whose body is holy
— it disqualifies her;
but this one, whose body is not holy
— it does not disqualify her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole קל וחומר from a כהנת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כהנת is disqualified because of her personal holiness, which a ישראלית does not have.

steps.title: The ban on marrying a כהן comes from a קל וחומר from a גרושה
steps.stepSummary: The extra word now teaches the son case, and the ban on כהונה is learned from a גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ban on marrying into כהונה comes from a קל וחומר from a divorcée. A divorcée may eat תרומה but may not marry a כהן. So this woman, who may not even eat תרומה, should surely be unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers step 11's question with a new source for the ban on marrying into כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roles switch. The extra word ״ובת״ covers the תרומה rule through her son, and a קל וחומר covers כהונה. A גרושה has the lighter status, since she may still eat תרומה, yet she is still banned from marrying a כהן, so this woman's stricter status means she is banned too.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman, forbidden to marry a כהן
'Is it not logical?' (the phrase that sums up a קל וחומר)
Unfit to marry into כהונה

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the complete source picture: an extra word for תרומה and logic for כהונה.

phrases.english: Rather, for the priesthood,
phrases.notes: He means the ban on marrying a כהן.

phrases.english: it is a kal vachomer from a divorcée:
Just as a divorcée, who is permitted to eat teruma,
— is forbidden to the priesthood,
this one, who is forbidden to eat teruma
— is it not logical that she is unfit for the priesthood?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 brings back the need for the extra word, the גמרא gives a new source for כהונה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that she may not marry into כהונה (from step 11).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from a גרושה, who may eat תרומה but is still forbidden to a כהן.

steps.title: Can we create a prohibition from logic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new source: a prohibition cannot be created through logic alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we give warnings (create prohibitions) from logic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר from step 16 with a general rule about how prohibitions are learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A punishable prohibition needs a warning written in the תורה. A prohibition built only from a קל וחומר is not accepted, so the source for the ban on כהונה seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Creating a prohibition (a warning) from logic alone, which is not allowed

phrases.english: But do we give warnings from logic?
phrases.notes: 'Logic' here means a קל וחומר. A punishable ban usually needs its own wording in the תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method used in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from a גרושה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Prohibitions cannot be created through logical derivation.

steps.title: It only reveals what was already included
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר does not create a new prohibition. It only shows how far the existing one reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is merely revealing the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 17. The logic is not making a new ban; it just reveals that she belongs in the already existing ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on a woman unfit for כהונה already exists in the תורה. The קל וחומר only tells us that this woman falls under it, so the rule against creating bans from logic does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Merely revealing the matter, not creating a new law

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: ״ובת״ teaches that she cannot eat תרומה through her son, and a קל וחומר from a גרושה reveals that she is unfit for כהונה.

phrases.english: It is merely a revealing of the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what the קל וחומר does: it reveals, it does not create.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר seemed to create a new prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only shows that she falls under an existing prohibition.

steps.title: Maybe 'unfit man' means only חייבי כריתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests limiting the rule to relations punishable by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that 'she had relations with a man unfit for her' means only those liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the sources are set, the גמרא asks which unfit men the rule is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that only the most severe forbidden relations, those punished with כרת, would cause this loss of status. Men who are only unfit to marry into ישראל, such as a ממזר, would not.

keyTerms.meaning: She had relations with a man unfit for her
Forbidden relations punished with כרת

phrases.english: But say that 'she had relations with one unfit for her'
— means those liable to karet,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from finding the source to defining which case the rule covers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The broad meaning of 'unfit man' in the rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Perhaps only the most severe relations, those punished with כרת, cause the disqualification.

steps.title: ״כי תהיה״ means men she could actually marry
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק speaks of a man she can marry, so it cannot mean חייבי כריתות, with whom marriage does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה said 'if she be married', meaning men with whom marriage can take effect. Those liable to כרת cannot have a marriage take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of step 19 using the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״כי תהיה״ describes a real marriage. With חייבי כריתות a marriage does not take effect, so the פסוק must be talking about other unfit men, such as those who are only unfit to marry into ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If she be married' (ויקרא 22:12)
A marriage that takes effect
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The words ״כי תהיה״ in רב's פסוק speak of men with whom a marriage takes effect. So רב's rule cannot be limited to חייבי כריתות. It also includes men who are only unfit for her.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'if she be [married]':
those with whom there can be marriage.
Those liable to karet cannot have marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Unfit man' might mean only חייבי כריתות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of men with whom marriage takes effect, which excludes חייבי כריתות.

steps.title: Then a gentile or slave should not disqualify her
steps.stepSummary: If the rule only covers a man she can marry, then a גוי or an עבד, whom she cannot marry, should not disqualify her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a gentile and a slave should not disqualify her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from the last step into a new problem. If only a man she can marry disqualifies her, then a גוי and an עבד should not disqualify her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא said the פסוק speaks of a man whose marriage with her takes effect, so it does not cover חייבי כריתות. But marriage with a גוי or an עבד also does not take effect. By that same reasoning they should not disqualify her, even though we know they do.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
A non-Jew
A slave (here, a non-Jewish slave)
They should disqualify (her)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a גוי or an עבד really fails to disqualify her. It is showing that the reasoning from step 20 seems to lead to a result we know is wrong.

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד לָא לִיפְסְלוּ!
phrases.english: If so, a gentile and a slave should not disqualify her!
phrases.notes: "If so" points back to step 20: only a man she can actually marry counts. She cannot marry a גוי or an עבד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד לָא לִיפְסְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 20 against itself: if only men she can marry count, a גוי and an עבד would be left out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 20 that the פסוק only covers a man whose marriage with her takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marriage with a גוי or an עבד does not take effect, just like with חייבי כריתות. So by the same logic they should not disqualify her, yet they do.

steps.title: They disqualify her through רבי ישמעאל's source
steps.stepSummary: A גוי and an עבד do disqualify her, but this is learned from a separate teaching of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: These disqualify her from the teaching of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a גוי and an עבד do disqualify her. This law does not come from our פסוק. It comes from a separate source, the teaching of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps its reading of our פסוק as speaking only of men she can marry. It explains the case of the גוי and the עבד with a different source. So there are now two sources, each covering a different group of men.

keyTerms.meaning: These (the ones just mentioned)
They disqualify

phrases.english: These disqualify her from the teaching of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate source: the case is covered by a different derivation, not by the פסוק under discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since our פסוק does not cover a גוי or an עבד, they would not disqualify her.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do disqualify her, based on רבי ישמעאל's separate derivation, while our פסוק still covers only men she can marry.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's source about a gentile or slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי ישמעאל: the source that a גוי or an עבד disqualifies a woman is the פסוק about a כהן's daughter who is widowed or divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: From where do we know that a gentile or a slave who had relations with a Jewish woman, a כהן's daughter, or a לוי's daughter disqualifies her? As it says: "But if a כהן's daughter becomes a widow or divorced…"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the teaching of רבי ישמעאל that it just mentioned. It gives the question and starts with the פסוק. The explanation of how the פסוק teaches this comes in the text that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's teaching covers every kind of Jewish woman: a regular Jewish woman, a כהן's daughter, and a לוי's daughter. All of them become disqualified after relations with a גוי or an עבד. His source is the words "widow" and "divorced" in the פסוק. How exactly those words prove it is explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
A כהן's daughter
A לוי's daughter
A widow and a divorced woman
And so on (the פסוק continues)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
From where do we know regarding a gentile or a slave
who had relations with a Jewish woman
or with a כהן's daughter or a לוי's daughter, that they have disqualified her?
phrases.notes: She becomes unfit to marry a כהן, and a כהן's daughter also loses her right to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "But if a כהן's daughter becomes
a widow or divorced, and so on"

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the source mentioned briefly in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי or an עבד who has relations with any Jewish woman (a regular Jewish woman, a כהן's daughter, or a לוי's daughter) disqualifies her. The source is the פסוק "ובת כהן כי תהיה אלמנה וגרושה."
